body:
Browser builds currently suppress the engine's worker threads. This change builds independent serial and pthread WebAssembly runtimes and selects threading when isolation, shared memory and worker graphics are available. Compute, gradients, previews and background saves use the same standard C++ worker code as native platforms. Browser adapters own DOM access, GPU context, audio delivery, WebSocket callbacks and persistent storage.

The release package contains versioned serial/threaded binaries, the capability loader, one verified shared asset payload and gzip sidecars. Unsupported hosts and initial threaded startup failures use the serial runtime. Public threaded hosting requires an HTTPS frontend with COOP/COEP; the optional `GLOB2_BROWSER_PUBLIC_URL` is checked before publication advertises it. Direct Google Cloud Storage links are explicitly labeled serial fallback.

Independent sub-agent review is complete, and its verified hosting finding is addressed. [Review report](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/30542d8329099973c6f0c1844675b1e8f82a4573/artifacts/threading-pr/evidence/review.json) and [validation inventory](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/30542d8329099973c6f0c1844675b1e8f82a4573/artifacts/threading-pr/evidence/validation.json) link the tested revision and coverage. [Evidence files](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/30542d8329099973c6f0c1844675b1e8f82a4573/artifacts/threading-pr/evidence) contain logs, raw checksum traces and native/browser scripting archives.

Validation:

- 137 build-system tests and 20 JavaScript unit tests passed; native compute, gradient and save-continuation cases passed.
- Twelve Chromium/Firefox/WebKit traces with serial and threaded 1/2/4-thread execution match macOS native for all 1,500 ticks. Four additional Chromium traces passed on the reviewed revision.
- All 33 native scripting cases passed. Both Chromium browser modes pass their corpus and match all 60 fresh native numeric, trace and decoded-save artifacts, with clean revision/provenance gates.
- Thread lifecycle, actual concurrent execution, PCM audio, shutdown and fallback checks pass across all three browsers. One Firefox startup timeout during concurrent local runs passed on isolated recheck; both results and the failure trace are retained.
- Hosted WebP decoding and the versioned production package's threaded, serial and startup-fallback modes passed.

Save/replay/network version gates are unchanged. Audio adds one PCM buffer of latency. Linux/Windows execution remains for CI; a live public HTTPS frontend and deployed TLS configuration were not exercised locally. Manual gameplay review is still required. The PR remains a draft while those checks and review proceed.
title: Enable real browser multithreading through shared engine workers
